evidence.detail: rs/L implements Runnable, accepts an InputStream plus volume and delay, converts the source AudioInputStream to PCM_SIGNED 16-bit audio, opens a javax.sound.sampled.Clip, starts playback, waits for completion and closes/flushes the clip and stream.

Playback obtains FloatControl.Type.MASTER_GAIN and maps the per-sound volume together with the global sound-level setting to a clamped linear amplitude and 20*log10 decibel value before applying the Clip gain control.

The constructor stores the requested delay and starts a dedicated Thread; run() sleeps that delay before Clip.start(), then monitors the global volume level while the clip is active and reapplies gain when it changes.

The class owns the global sound-level state used by playback. Its static level setter emits ::soundoff for level 4 or ::soundon otherwise through the client command path before storing the new level, while another helper can provide a byte[] audio source.
Client is the only exact-v308 external class with a direct rs/L type reference, fixing this as the client sound-effect playback helper rather than a general media utility.

Multiple historical RSPS clients preserve a custom class named SoundPlayer with the same Runnable + AudioInputStream + Java Sound Clip/MASTER_GAIN playback shape. This source family is corroborative only; exact-v308 bytecode is primary authority.

proposals.note: SoundPlayer is strongly corroborated historical RSPS terminology for this exact Java Sound playback role. The name does not imply that the class owns music/MIDI playback, which remains a separate subsystem.
